steps.title: What is an Array?
steps.content: An array is a collection of elements of the same type stored at contiguous memory locations. Each element is accessed by its index (position).
steps.example: arr = [10, 20, 30, 40, 50]. arr[0] = 10, arr[2] = 30. Indexing starts at 0.
steps.tip: Array access is O(1) — instant. But insertion/deletion in the middle is O(n) because elements must shift.

steps.title: Access Elements
steps.explanation: arr[3] accesses the element at index 3, which is the 4th element: 20. Remember: indexing starts at 0.

steps.title: Array Traversal
steps.prompt: What is the time complexity of traversing all elements of an array of size n?
steps.explanation: We must visit each element exactly once, so the time complexity is O(n).

steps.title: Common Array Operations
steps.content: Common operations: Search (O(n) linear, O(log n) binary if sorted), Insert at end (O(1) amortized), Insert in middle (O(n) due to shifting), Delete from middle (O(n) due to shifting).
steps.example: Inserting at index 2 in [1, 2, 3, 4] requires shifting elements at indices 2 and 3 rightward: [1, 2, new, 3, 4].

steps.title: Two-Pointer Preview
steps.prompt: To find if a pair of numbers in a sorted array sums to a target, which technique is most efficient?
steps.explanation: Two pointers (left at start, right at end) can find a pair in O(n) for sorted arrays. Move left pointer forward if sum < target, right pointer backward if sum > target.

questions.prompt: What is the time complexity of accessing an element by index in an array?
questions.explanation: Array access by index is O(1) because the memory address is calculated directly: base_address + index × element_size.

questions.prompt: Which operation is most expensive on an array?
questions.explanation: Inserting in the middle requires shifting all subsequent elements, making it O(n). Accessing first/last elements and updating are O(1).

srs_cards.question: What is the time complexity of array operations: access, insert at end, insert in middle, delete from middle?
srs_cards.answer: Access: O(1), insert at end: O(1) amortized, insert in middle: O(n), delete from middle: O(n).
